learningObjectives: Explain the structure and purpose of lambda expressions.
Identify and use common functional interfaces.
Convert simple anonymous implementations into lambda-based expressions.

activities.title: Lambda Anatomy
activities.instruction: Explore each part of a lambda expression.

content.concept: A lambda expression provides a compact implementation of a functional interface. Its syntax can contain parameters, the arrow operator, and an expression or statement body.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: The lambda parameters receiving input values.
The lambda operator separating parameters from the body.
The expression that produces the result.
A complete lambda expression implementing compatible functional behavior.
A functional interface whose method accepts two values and produces a result.

activities.title: Functional Interface Matcher
activities.instruction: Match common functional interfaces with the behavior they represent.

content.concept: A functional interface has exactly one abstract method. Common interfaces include Predicate for boolean tests, Function for transforming a value, Consumer for accepting a value without returning one, and Supplier for producing a value.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

choices: Predicate<T> → tests a value and returns boolean
Function<T,R> → transforms a value into another value
Consumer<T> → accepts a value and returns no result
Supplier<T> → supplies a value without an input
config.answer: Predicate<T> → tests a value and returns boolean

activities.title: Lambda Builder
activities.instruction: Build a lambda that checks whether a number is positive.

content.concept: Lambda syntax can replace simple anonymous implementations when a functional interface is expected. Parameter types can often be inferred from the target functional interface.

activities.title: Method Reference Selector
activities.instruction: Choose the method reference that is equivalent to each lambda.

content.concept: A method reference uses the :: operator to refer directly to an existing compatible method. It can make lambda-based code shorter when the lambda simply delegates to an existing method.
